# Expected values for lm_math_fi_pkg.f_lm_quantize, replayed by
# sim/generic_domain/tb_quantize_vectors.vhd.
#
# PURPOSE
#   Pins the arithmetic of f_lm_quantize across the format domain, so that a
#   future edit to the function - including one made while adding a new
#   generic-domain check - cannot change the result for a legal configuration
#   without failing the gate.
#
# HOW THESE WERE PRODUCED
#   Two groups, both checked against the same independent reference.
#
#   Group 1, geometry (6,2) -> (4,1), 4608 vectors.
#     Originally emitted by simulating src/lm_math_fi_pkg.vhd as it stood at
#     commit 07345f1bc07a (the tip of main before the generic-domain work) under GHDL.
#     That differential run reported all 4608 combinations bit-identical
#     between the pre-change and post-change package.
#
#   Group 2, the degenerate binary-point region, 12096 vectors.
#     Computed by an exact-integer reference implementation written from the
#     documented semantics using arbitrary-precision integers only - no floating
#     point, and no code from the VHDL, the Python model or the JavaScript port.
#     A stored word R with binary point B denotes the exact rational R / 2**B,
#     with R read as two's complement when the format is signed; the quotient is
#     rounded under the selected mode and then clamped or wrapped into the
#     destination format.
#
#   The same reference was required to reproduce every one of Group 1's values
#   before Group 2 was emitted, so the two groups agree on the region where they
#   overlap and neither was produced by the code under test.
#
#   Regenerating these is a deliberate act: it re-baselines the arithmetic. Do it
#   only when a behaviour change is intended, and say so in the changelog.
#
# COVERAGE
#   Group 1: all 64 values of a 6-bit input
#     x 2 source signednesses   (C_LM_UNSIGNED = 1, C_LM_SIGNED = 2)
#     x 2 target signednesses
#     x 9 rounding modes        (C_LM_TRUNC_BITS = 0 .. C_LM_ROUND_AWAY = 8)
#     x 2 overflow modes        (C_LM_SATURATE = 1, C_LM_WRAP = 2)
#
#   Group 2: the same signedness, rounding and overflow sweep over every input
#   value of each of the following geometries, which Group 1 does not reach:
#     (4,4) -> (4,4)   binary point equal to the width, both sides
#     (4,4) -> (4,0)   binary point equal to the width, narrowing
#     (4,0) -> (4,4)   binary point equal to the width, widening
#     (4,6) -> (4,2)   binary point above the width, source only
#     (4,2) -> (4,6)   binary point above the width, destination only
#     (4,8) -> (4,6)   binary point above the width, both sides
#     (4,8) -> (4,0)   disjoint bit weights, destination entirely above
#     (4,0) -> (4,8)   disjoint bit weights, destination entirely below
#     (4,4) -> (4,1)   exactly one bit of weight overlap
#     (1,0) -> (1,0)   width 1, no fractional bits
#     (1,1) -> (1,1)   width 1, binary point equal to the width
#     (1,1) -> (4,3)   width 1 source into a wider destination
#     (4,3) -> (1,1)   width 1 destination from a wider source
#     (1,3) -> (2,1)   width 1, binary point above the width
#
#   The four alias constants share a value with one of the nine rounding modes,
#   so they are covered by the value they alias.
#
# FORMAT
#   Lines beginning with '#' are comments. Every other line is one vector:
#     old_width old_binpnt old_arith new_width new_binpnt new_arith
#     rounding overflow value expected
#   where `value` and `expected` are unsigned integer renderings of the source
#   and destination bit patterns, and `old_arith` / `new_arith` are
#   C_LM_UNSIGNED (1) or C_LM_SIGNED (2).
